title: Fold-Matched Local Residual Correction for Cross-Fitted Composition Stacks on Small Matbench Tasks

intervention_object.acts_on: the out-of-fold residuals of a cross-fitted stack of composition experts, as they are transferred from training compositions to a query and added to the stack's prediction
intervention_object.operator: a fold-matched analogue estimate (neighbour label plus the neighbour-excluded refit's predicted difference between query and neighbour), blended with the full-refit stack prediction by a damping map over support descriptors that is fit on deployment-matched instances manufactured from pair-excluded refits inside the training fold
intervention_object.decision_variables: the damping value lambda(s_q) per query (from a low-capacity admissible family that contains lambda = 0), plus the nested-CV-selected kernel bandwidth h, neighbourhood size k_nn, composition distance rho, residual scale tau and expert set E

hook: We construct a fold-matched local residual correction for cross-fitted composition stacks whose damping is fit on deployment-matched instances, because the naive out-of-fold correction should hurt most at the near-duplicate end of composition space, not at the off-support end that novelty damping guards. The reason is that a neighbour's out-of-fold residual double-counts an error that the refit stack has already absorbed by training on that neighbour.
hook_shape_rationale: (i) Shape (a). The named metric is outer-test MAE (and log loss / probability AUROC on the classification tasks), stratified by the distance delta_1 from each test composition to its nearest training composition. The prediction that the naive correction's excess error over the uncorrected stack concentrates in the smallest-delta_1 stratum, and grows with an expert's capacity to interpolate its training points, is the opposite of the off-support failure that the Δ-model leaf (semanticscholar:398586587c1f70079b3b60825e93ff651a519ff9) and every distance-based damping scheme anticipate. (ii) Shape (b) was viable, by citing the stacking substrate's tacit assumption that level-1 inputs from out-of-fold models are interchangeable with full-refit outputs, but that mismatch is a known (if usually ignored) property of stacking, so reframing it louder would not pass the unnamed-in-practice test; the non-obvious content is where along the support axis it bites for a local correction, which is an empirical direction claim. (iii) Because nested-CV tuning of the naive registers a mirrored double-count at near-duplicate pairs that straddle inner folds and can respond only by shrinking its whole distance-decay schedule, a tuned naive may show little or no excess; the direction claim is therefore also carried by the fixed-schedule naive arm (A1f against A2a in falsification_prediction, differing only in M_q), with the tuned naive's selected damping strength reported.

gap_closure.gap: (additive; leaf sites L_deltamodel, L_restgp, L_concrete_residual) No residual-correction leaf provides a correction whose expected effect is non-negative where local reference evidence is thin. The Δ-model leaf finds corrections are needed most exactly where training coverage is sparsest, but it relies on acquiring new labels there. The residual-GP and physics-residual leaves say nothing about what their correction does to a query with no close training analogue. A fixed offline benchmark offers no label acquisition, so the question is open in exactly the regime where it matters. — stakes: on steels (n = 312) a handful of atypical alloys dominate MAE, so a correction that extrapolates wrongly there erases or reverses the average gain. In discovery use, the novel compositions are the ones whose predictions are acted on, so a correction that is harmful off-support costs real experiments.
gap_closure.sub_pattern_not_applicable_reason: No sub-cluster under assumption_audit_and_pivot delivers a runnable residual-correction mechanism. C01 relocates a security/detection locus. C05 proves identifiability. C11 pivots a budgeted choice rule. C19 re-derives a statistical certificate and would force an unrequested bound. C28 targets distributed protocols and C29 convergence rates. Parent-only fit is used.
gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin in this domain (all sub-cluster exemplars are from distant fields), so the gap is closed at parent level in two halves. The framing move audits the premise that a neighbour's out-of-fold residual is exchangeable with the refit stack's residual at the query, and pivots it into a fold-matched analogue transfer computed from refits that excluded the neighbour. The companion's deliverable is a set of deployment-matched instances, built from pair-excluded refits inside the training fold, on which the damping map lambda(s) is fit with lambda = 0 admissible. This gives a correction whose in-fold realised effect, aggregated over the manufactured instances, is non-negative by construction without any label acquisition; per support regime the same holds only where the family Lambda can represent the regime boundary, which is why the evaluation stratifies by delta_1.

core_mechanism: Notation. Fix an official Matbench v0.1 outer fold k with training set T_k; all objects below are computed from T_k only. Partition T_k at random into J inner folds P_1..P_J (J an integer, at least 3, chosen once on the cost-variance trade-off and reported); m(j) denotes the inner fold of training composition j. A cross-fitted stack F combines experts e in E (admissible members: gradient-boosted trees or random forest on Magpie features, MODNet on MatMiner features, TabPFN v2 on Magpie features run on CPU, kNN on element-fraction vectors; E chosen by nested CV) with non-negative level-1 weights beta fit on inner out-of-fold predictions (Breiman NNLS for regression, a non-negative logistic level-1 for classification). This stack is substrate, not contribution. Write F^full for the stack whose experts are refit on all of T_k, F^(-m) for the one whose experts saw T_k minus P_m, and F^(-m,-m') for the pair-excluded refit that saw T_k minus (P_m union P_m'). The level-1 weights beta are fit once on the out-of-fold predictions of all of T_k and held fixed in F^(-m) and F^(-m,-m'). Residuals live on a scale tau chosen by nested CV (raw target for regression; probability or logit working residual for classification), and r_j = y_j - F^(-m(j))(x_j) is j's out-of-fold residual. Audited premise. The naive local out-of-fold correction predicts F^full(x_q) + sum_j w_qj r_j, with kernel weights w_qj = K(rho(q,j)/h) normalised over the k_nn nearest training compositions under a composition distance rho (admissible: Element Mover's Distance via the ElMD package, or Euclidean on standardised Magpie vectors). This silently assumes that r_j estimates the deployed stack's error at q. Algebraically, the naive estimate equals A_q + M_q, where A_q = sum_j w_qj a_qj with per-neighbour analogue estimates a_qj = F^(-m(j))(x_q) + r_j is a fold-matched analogue estimate (each a_qj is the neighbour label y_j plus the neighbour-excluded refit's predicted difference F^(-m(j))(x_q) - F^(-m(j))(x_j) between query and neighbour). The absorption term M_q = sum_j w_qj [F^full(x_q) - F^(-m(j))(x_q)] measures how much the deployed refit has already moved toward the neighbours it was trained on. For a near-duplicate neighbour and an interpolating expert (trees, TabPFN in-context prediction), M_q is close to r_j, so the naive correction applies the neighbour's error twice. That failure sits where support is densest; a distance-monotone novelty schedule damps the opposite end, so it can suppress the near-duplicate double-count only by shrinking the whole correction, including where the correction helps. Pivot (the runnable fix). Predict yhat_q = (1 - lambda(s_q)) F^full(x_q) + lambda(s_q) A_q. In A_q the experts behind the base prediction, the transfer and the borrowed residual all come from a refit that saw neither q nor j, so M_q is removed rather than damped. Here s_q = (delta_1, n_eff, sigma_A) is a support descriptor: delta_1 is rho to the nearest training composition, n_eff = (sum of unnormalised kernel masses)^2 / (sum of squared masses), and sigma_A is the w-weighted standard deviation of the per-neighbour analogue estimates a_qj (equivalently of y_j plus the transfer F^(-m(j))(x_q) - F^(-m(j))(x_j)), so it reflects neighbour-label disagreement as well as transfer disagreement. The damping lambda maps s to [0, lambda_max] with lambda_max at most 1, drawn from a low-capacity admissible family Lambda (logistic in s with sign constraints, or isotonic in n_eff) that contains lambda = 0. Manufactured signal (the companion). The deployment-optimal damping in Lambda (the family-restricted target defined in the ESTIMAND of core_mechanism_reasoning) cannot be estimated from out-of-fold residuals alone, because those do not stand in the deployed fold relation. So for every i in P_m the stack builds a deployment-matched instance: the 'deployed' prediction is F^(-m)(x_i); the analogue A_i = sum over j outside P_m of w_ij [F^(-m,-m(j))(x_i) + y_j - F^(-m,-m(j))(x_j)] uses refits that excluded both i's and j's folds; s_i is computed against T_k minus P_m, with sigma_A taken over the same per-neighbour terms. Then i relates to F^(-m) exactly as an outer test composition relates to F^full, up to the training set being one inner fold smaller. Both this statement and 'saw neither q nor j' hold at the expert level: because beta is fit once and held fixed, they assume that beta's low-capacity dependence on the excluded folds' labels is negligible. Lambda, h, k_nn, rho and tau are fit or selected by minimising the realised loss of (1 - lambda(s_i)) F^(-m)(x_i) + lambda(s_i) A_i on these instances, with selection cross-validated grouped by m. Because lambda = 0 is admissible, the selected correction's realised in-fold effect, aggregated over the manufactured instances, is non-negative relative to the uncorrected stack by construction (empirical grade; per support regime it holds only where Lambda can represent the regime boundary, and its transfer to outer test is the falsification target), with no new labels acquired. As A becomes noisy relative to the stack, the fitted lambda shrinks toward 0 but need not reach it: when A's error is large but not positively correlated with the stack's, the population-optimal lambda shrinks toward 0 without reaching it (it is strictly positive for independent mean-zero errors). The correction is switched off (lambda identically 0) exactly when the grouped-CV realised gain of every non-zero member of Lambda is non-positive, so 'switches off' means 'is selected at 0 by the grouped CV'.
core_mechanism_reasoning: BLOCK 1 — PREMISES. (P1) The out-of-fold errors of global composition stacks on these tasks co-vary within chemical neighbourhoods. Reason: Matbench composition data are chemically clustered and redundant (arxiv:2005.00707), and correction need tracks local coverage (semanticscholar:398586587c1f70079b3b60825e93ff651a519ff9). Untested on these tasks — falsification target, because if it is false A_q carries no signal and lambda collapses to 0. (P2) Interpolating experts absorb their training neighbours, so M_q is large exactly when delta_1 is small. Reason: tree ensembles and in-context TabPFN predict near-duplicates of training points close to those points' labels. Untested — falsification target and the load-bearing bet of the hook. (P3, OBSERVATION MODEL) Outer test compositions are drawn from T_k's dataset by the official random 5-fold split, so a test composition's neighbourhood in T_k, and its fold relation to F^full, are distributed like a manufactured instance's neighbourhood in T_k minus P_m and its fold relation to F^(-m). The residual biases are (a) a one-fold-smaller training set, which slightly lowers near-duplicate density and raises base error in manufactured instances, and (b) correlated instances, because a composition appears as a neighbour in many instances. (a) is the same small-sample shift every nested CV tolerates; (b) is handled by grouping selection by m, which removes reuse of a held-out instance's target but not all coupling: labels of the held-out fold still enter training-fold instances as neighbour labels y_j inside A_i, a weak dependence the grouped CV does not remove. The premise would be false under a cluster or chemical-system split, so the claim is scoped to the official random folds. Untested — falsification target via the near-duplicate stratum. (P4) The residual scale tau keeps the transfer meaningful for classification. Reason: additive transfer on the probability scale can leave [0,1], so the logit working residual is admissible and the choice is made by nested CV. ESTIMAND: the expected per-composition loss (absolute error; log loss for classification) of yhat on compositions drawn as the official outer test fold is drawn from the task dataset, overall and conditional on delta_1 stratum. The damping's target is the family-restricted minimiser of the s-averaged loss, lambda_Lambda = argmin over lambda in Lambda of E[loss(y, (1 - lambda(s)) F^full + lambda(s) A)] under that same draw, which is what step 8 of core_mechanism_steps minimises on the manufactured instances under P3. It coincides with the pointwise conditional minimiser lambda*(s) = argmin over l in [0, lambda_max] of E[loss(y, (1 - l) F^full + l A) | s] whenever that minimiser lies in Lambda. BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT. Naive version: add the kernel-weighted out-of-fold residuals of the k_nn nearest training compositions to the full-refit stack prediction, scaled by a novelty damping that decays with distance, and tune h, k_nn and the decay by nested CV on out-of-fold residuals. Branch (i): it relies on the false premise that a neighbour's out-of-fold residual is the deployed refit's error at the query (M_q = 0). Under random folds on redundant data with interpolating experts, M_q is largest at the near-duplicate end, so the naive correction double-counts there. Its out-of-fold tuning signal is not blind to this: for a cross-fold neighbour j of a tuning point i, the tuning-time absorption term is F^(-m(i))(x_i) - F^(-m(j))(x_i), where the first model saw j and the second saw i, so tuning registers a mirrored double-count at near-duplicate pairs that straddle inner folds. A distance-monotone damping can respond to that only by shrinking its whole decay schedule, so the tuned naive either keeps part of the near-duplicate double-count or gives up the correction elsewhere, up to switching off entirely (then it equals the uncorrected stack). The naive's failure is therefore that a distance-monotone damping cannot remove the near-duplicate double-count while keeping the correction elsewhere, not that the tuning signal is blind to it. The mechanism confronts this by removing M_q through fold matching and by fitting the damping on instances that reproduce the deployed fold relation. STANDARD-TOOL FOLLOW-UP: the confrontation borrows cross-fitting (as in double machine learning) and stacking's out-of-fold discipline. The domain-specific structure that the textbook tools do not solve is the coupling of two points' fold memberships, query and borrowed neighbour, in one estimate under compositional redundancy. That coupling forces pair-excluded refits F^(-m,-m'), both for the transfer and for the instances on which the damping is fit; ordinary cross-fitting excludes only the evaluated point. Avoided lineage nodes: the transfer is not regression-kriging or Δ-learning (n_residual_on_input), which borrow in-sample or never-fit residuals; the damping is not partial pooling (C_shrinkage) or an applicability-domain cut-off (C_applicability_domain), since its value is learned from manufactured deployment-matched loss and need not decrease with distance; and no per-query expert weighting is introduced (C_moe, C_des). BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE. (a) Anchor-only, because the remaining gaps ask for measurements, which are placed as strata and arms of the falsification rather than as mechanism legs. (b) Alternatives rejected: using in-sample residuals instead (they vanish for interpolating experts, so the correction disappears); averaging the J fold models at test time instead of refitting (this removes M_q for the base prediction but leaves the damping tuned on mismatched instances, and lowers base accuracy at n = 312); a learned per-query gate over experts (lands on C_moe and overfits at this n); a variance-formula shrinkage (cannot represent the near-duplicate failure, because the variance of A is smallest exactly there).
core_mechanism_steps: 1. For outer fold k, load T_k from the official Matbench v0.1 split via the matbench package; compute Magpie and MatMiner composition features (matminer) and element-fraction vectors; never touch the outer test labels until step 11. 2. Partition T_k into J random inner folds; for each expert in the candidate pool of admissible experts, train on T_k minus P_m for each m to get out-of-fold predictions. This out-of-fold part is all that step 3 consumes. 3. Select the expert set E by grouped inner CV (grouped by m) on the stack's out-of-fold loss, fitting the level-1 weights of each candidate set inside that grouped CV from the step-2 out-of-fold predictions only. This runs immediately after step 2 and before the level-1 fit for the selected E and before steps 5-8, so the pair-excluded refits are run only for the selected E. Report the selection outcome and its grouped-CV dispersion. 4. For the selected E, fit the non-negative level-1 weights beta once on the out-of-fold predictions of all of T_k, form F^(-m) and the out-of-fold residuals r_j on each candidate scale tau, and refit all experts in E on T_k to form F^full. 5. For each unordered inner-fold pair (m, m'), refit each expert in E on T_k minus (P_m union P_m') and keep beta fixed, giving F^(-m,-m'); store its predictions on P_m and P_m' (the only points it is ever evaluated at); this is the dominant CPU cost and is parallelised over pairs and experts on the 24 cores. 6. Compute pairwise composition distances under each admissible rho (ElMD; Euclidean on standardised Magpie) between all training compositions, and between each outer test composition and T_k. 7. Build deployment-matched instances: for each i in P_m, take its k_nn nearest compositions outside P_m, compute kernel weights with bandwidth h, the per-neighbour analogue estimates and their weighted sum A_i from F^(-m,-m(j)) as defined in core_mechanism, the competing prediction F^(-m)(x_i), and the support descriptor s_i (with sigma_A the w-weighted standard deviation of the per-neighbour analogue estimates); output a table of (A_i, F^(-m)(x_i), s_i, y_i, m) for every training composition and every candidate (rho, h, k_nn, tau) that step 8 searches over. 8. Fit the damping map: for each candidate (rho, h, k_nn, tau, family in Lambda), fit lambda on instances from all but one inner fold m by minimising the realised loss of (1 - lambda(s)) F^(-m) + lambda(s) A, and score on the held-out m; select the configuration with the lowest grouped-CV loss, with the lambda = 0 configuration always in the candidate set; refit the selected lambda on all instances. 9. Deployment for outer test composition q: compute the per-neighbour analogue estimates and A_q from the stored F^(-m(j)) predictions at x_q (each inner fold model predicts q once) and the r_j of its k_nn nearest training compositions, compute s_q against T_k, and output yhat_q = (1 - lambda(s_q)) F^full(x_q) + lambda(s_q) A_q. This changes the submitted prediction, and hence the fold MAE or AUROC, only where the fitted lambda is non-zero. 10. For classification, map yhat_q back to a probability (inverse link when tau is the logit scale, clipping when it is the probability scale), and choose the hard-label threshold inside T_k by the same grouped CV for the balanced-accuracy report. 11. Score yhat on the outer test fold once; record per-composition delta_1 and M_q (the absorption term, computable from the stored predictions) for the stratified analysis; repeat for all five official folds and four tasks.
falsification_prediction: (a) Procedure: on the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks with official folds, compare arm A0 (the cross-fitted stack F^full), A1 (the naive novelty-damped local out-of-fold correction, all of its knobs tuned by nested CV on out-of-fold residuals), and A2 (the proposed fold-matched correction with manufactured damping). Two ablations: A2a (fold-matched transfer with A1's distance damping) and A2b (naive transfer, which adds M_q back, with damping fit on manufactured instances). A further arm, A1f, applies the naive transfer (which retains M_q) under the damping schedule selected for A2a, so that A1f and A2a differ only in M_q; A1's nested-CV-selected damping strength is reported alongside A1. Score once per outer fold, and stratify outer-test errors by quantile bins of delta_1 (number of bins a reporting choice, fixed before scoring). (b) If the candidate works: A1's error excess over A0 is concentrated in the smallest-delta_1 stratum and is larger when E contains interpolating experts. A2's MAE (and log loss on expt_is_metal and glass, where both probability AUROC and in-fold-thresholded balanced accuracy are reported separately) is no worse than A0 in every delta_1 stratum, with any gain concentrated in intermediate-support strata; A2 is no worse than A1 overall. A1f's outer-test MAE excess over A2a is concentrated in the smallest-delta_1 stratum, which exposes M_q even when nested-CV tuning shrinks A1's damping to off (in which case A1 equals A0 and its excess cannot appear). (c) Load-bearing variable: the absorption term M_q. Negative control: A2b reinjects M_q while keeping everything else of A2. The prediction is that outer-test MAE in the smallest-delta_1 stratum moves from A2's level back toward A1's, and that the fitted lambda shrinks there, losing A2's intermediate-support gain. A label-permutation control (permute y within each inner fold before building the manufactured instances) should drive the selected lambda to 0 and return the downstream MAE to A0's. The within-inner-fold permuted labels are used for every expert fit, refit, out-of-fold residual and level-1 weight from step 2 onward, not only inside the manufactured instances, which is consistent with permuting before building them. Positive control: restrict E to a non-interpolating expert (ridge on Magpie features), where M_q is small by construction; there A1 and A2 should give nearly equal downstream MAE, which isolates M_q as the cause of the A1-A2 difference. All differences are reported per task with fold-level dispersion and a variance-corrected resampled test (Nadeau-Bengio); no numeric gain bar is asserted.
compute_budget: 0 GPU-day, since CPU-only is a hard user constraint, and $0 API. CPU cost on the 24-core workstation is dominated by the pair-excluded refits (J(J-1)/2 per selected expert per outer fold), especially CPU TabPFN v2 on glass and expt_is_metal. A rough estimate is on the order of a few CPU-days for the full four-task campaign including iteration, and much less if TabPFN is excluded by the nested expert selection. Comfortable against the 2-4 week window.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Their GPR Δ-model corrects a universal potential that was never fit to the correction's reference points, and it acquires new DFT labels where support is thin. We construct a correction for a base stack fit on the very compositions whose residuals are borrowed: it removes the resulting absorption term by pair-excluded refits, and it learns where to damp the correction toward zero from manufactured deployment-matched instances, with no label acquisition.

MatterVial fuses latent and symbolic features into one global MODNet and never models the residual it leaves. We add a post-hoc correction stage acting on the out-of-fold residuals of a stack (which may include a MODNet expert), and predict and test where along the nearest-neighbour-distance axis such a stage helps or harms on the same official folds.

ECSG stacks composition experts with one global level-1 rule and no residual stage (abstract-only inference). We keep a global non-negative stack as substrate and construct a fold-matched local residual correction on top of it for the small experimental Matbench tasks.

ICL-FM runs one TabPFN predictor per task on GPU. We use TabPFN on CPU only as one admissible expert, and identify its in-context interpolation of near-duplicate training compositions as a source of the absorption term that makes a naive out-of-fold residual correction double-count.

CORE-STACK+ learns a per-sample gate over experts with large vision pools. We leave expert weights global and learn only a low-capacity per-query damping of a residual transfer, fit on manufactured instances so that it is estimable at n of a few hundred under nested selection.

Matbench fixes random 5-fold splits and nested-CV reference pipelines. We show that, under exactly those random folds, the fold relation between a deployed refit and borrowed out-of-fold residuals is what a local correction must match, and we stratify the evaluation by test-to-train distance, which the protocol leaves uncontrolled.

DSBM assigns each instance a hard best classifier through a meta-model (abstract-only inference). We make no per-instance expert choice and instead blend a fold-matched analogue estimate with one stack prediction by a damping that grouped CV on manufactured deployment-matched instances selects at zero when no non-zero member of its admissible family has positive realised gain.

CRC gates a post-hoc residual corrector on time-series forecasters with a causality-inspired encoder and safety rules so that correction does not degrade reliable base predictions (abstract-only inference); its base forecaster is not trained on the points whose residuals the corrector borrows. Our increment is the absorption term that arises when it is: we remove it from the transfer by pair-excluded refits and fit the damping on manufactured deployment-matched instances, so non-degradation is an aggregate in-fold property of selecting over a family that contains lambda = 0, not a safety rule.

what_step_was_missed: Their Δ-model corrects a base model (CHGNet) trained on different data from the reference points whose residuals the GP borrows, so the borrowed residuals are exchangeable with the query's residual by construction, and thin support is handled by acquiring labels. For the correction to work when the base predictor is trained on the very points whose residuals it borrows, and no labels can be acquired, two further constructions are needed, and they built neither: pair-excluded refits that remove the absorption term from the transfer, and deployment-matched instances on which to learn where the correction must be damped toward zero (and whether grouped CV selects it at zero).
composition_note: Anchor-only selection with one Step 2a chain companion; the five remaining gaps are deferred, and their measurements (error-structure stratification, selection variance, hard-label versus probability scoring, near-neighbour dependence) appear only as arms or strata inside falsification_prediction.
